newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin takes gentle swipe at NATO summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin takes gentle swipe at NATO summit.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, in a gentle swipe at NATO plans to expand, said on Saturday he much preferred the temperate climes of his Russian holiday home to the hot-house Alliance summit host Madrid.
Yeltsin noted visiting Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari had said on arrival he found the temperature far more agreeable in Karelia, northwestern Russia, than in the Spanish capital.
"I also like the climate here," Yeltsin told reporters, pausing meaningfully for effect. "I like it significantly more than (the temperature) in Madrid."
It was Yeltsin's first public comment on Madrid since the summit. He did not specifically mention NATO.
Russia has made no secret of its displeasure about NATO's invitation at the summit this week to the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to join the defence alliance.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov described the move on Tuesday as "the biggest mistake in Europe since the end of World War Two". But overall Moscow's response has been relatively muted.
Neutral Finland says it will work closely with NATO but has no immediate plans to try to join the alliance.
